newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN PRISONERS RECEIVE PRIVATE HEALTH CARE.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN PRISONERS RECEIVE PRIVATE HEALTH CARE.

text.p: Nearly three quarters of South Africa's prisoners received private health care during 1996 at a cost to the state of over 29.5 million rand, Correctional Services Minister Sipo Mzimela said on Tuesday.
Mzimela said in a written response to a question that 89,389 out of the average 118,400 prison population were treated by private doctors.
"Health care services are made available to prisoners by the government as far as possible," Mzimela said.

"However, should these services be insufficient, then at the discretion of the treating medical officer...a prisoner patient may be referred for appropriate consultation or medical treatment to doctors or private facilities."
